subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a shared async lifecycle ResourceManager-style protocol across agent, gateway, session, and plugin cleanup paths, or continue with localized lifecycle helpers?
rationale: The remaining work changes an owner boundary and likely a public plugin/runtime contract; source inspection shows the motivating bugs have targeted fixes but no shared shutdown protocol exists yet.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow design first
options.body: Define the shutdown semantics, owner boundary, and representative proof matrix before any implementation PR adds a new shared lifecycle API.

options.title: Keep localized helpers
options.body: Close or defer the broad ResourceManager idea and continue fixing lifecycle races within the owning subsystem as they appear.

options.title: Plugin-SDK-only experiment
options.body: Limit the next step to a backward-compatible plugin SDK lifecycle primitive and avoid changing agent/session internals until proven necessary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow design first
recommendation.body: Define the shutdown semantics, owner boundary, and representative proof matrix before any implementation PR adds a new shared lifecycle API.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central helper blame and root repository policy route broad SDK/runtime design choices toward current-main owners rather than a single contributor proposal.
